name: Radix Sort
description: Sorts integers by processing each digit from least significant to most significant, using a stable sort (counting sort) at each digit position. Linear time for fixed-width integers.
aim: Sort by digit: perform stable counting sort on units digit, then tens, then hundreds, etc. Since counting sort is stable, relative order from previous passes is preserved.
howItWorks: Find maximum value to determine number of digits d
For each digit position (ones, tens, hundreds…)
Apply counting sort using only that digit as the key
Stable sort preserves order from previous digit passes
After processing all digits, array is fully sorted

time.bestCase: d = number of digits, k = base (usually 10)
time.averageCase: Linear in n for fixed number of digits

complexity.spaceDescription: Auxiliary arrays for each digit pass

realWorld: Sorting IP addresses and MAC addresses
Sorting large datasets of integers with known range
whenToUse: Integers with a fixed number of digits
Keys can be decomposed into digits or characters
alternatives: Counting Sort — simpler for single-pass integer sorting
Bucket Sort — better for floating-point uniform distributions
Merge/Quick Sort — when digit decomposition is expensive
